U-turn at Nvidia: Jensen Huang returns as head of the company eleven days after resigning, the stock jumps more than 30% and the Nasdaq 6%

On Monday, November 23, Nvidia's board restored Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board member, eleven days after his resignation. Donald Trump, who had called for his return, hailed a "correct" decision. The stock jumped more than 30% at the open, lifting all of Wall Street [1][2][3][6].

The board voted unanimously to bring back Jensen Huang, the company's co-founder, as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, "after a series of discussions and meetings" that satisfied it of his "candor" and "ability to lead" [3][6].
The board says it received input from "senior levels" of the U.S. government and is "confident" that Huang's return poses no national security risk [3][6].

It is a U-turn: as recently as November 17, board chair Harvey Jones indicated that Nvidia did not intend to bring him back [4][6]. Huang had resigned on November 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence was concerned about [4][9].

Colette Kress, the chief financial officer who served as interim CEO, remains CFO, and Harvey Jones stays on as board chair [3]. A board committee is still investigating whether foreign intelligence services targeted Huang [2].

On Truth Social, Donald Trump called the decision "correct and proper" and said Washington had "no reason to believe" there was a national security risk; according to him, Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed there is no evidence of unlawful conduct by Huang [6]. He asked Nvidia to continue its internal investigation into compliance with export controls [6].
Trump also called Huang a "great patriot" and a "national treasure", and said he had spoken to board members [7][8]. Elon Musk reacted on X: "the mistake has been corrected" [7].

At Wall Street's open, Nvidia stock gained more than 30%, according to Euronews, and as much as 33% according to CNBC [1][2]. The Nasdaq climbed 6%, the S&P 500 4% and the Dow Jones 1,186 points (+2.5%); according to the Wall Street Journal, cited by Quartz, Nvidia could add $1 trillion in value in a single session, a record [5].
The key point: the head of the heaviest company on the world's stock markets is returning with the direct backing of the White House, and all of Wall Street is rebounding with him [1][5][6].

The rebound comes in the middle of the AI stock crash: between its record on October 6 ($5.78 trillion in value) and the close on November 17, Nvidia had lost $2.03 trillion [10]. This Monday, the stock recovered part of that fall within minutes [1][5].

The return is also political. As recently as Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent refused to back Huang's return and was still waiting for Nvidia's answers about AI chips that ended up in China [11]. Donald Trump's line has prevailed [6][8].
The underlying questions remain open: the board's investigation into possible targeting by a foreign intelligence service, and compliance with export rules to China, which Trump wants pursued [2][6].

Nvidia weighs so heavily in the major indices that its surge lifts most equity funds, including the "world" or "S&P 500" ETFs held in savings and retirement accounts. After weeks of decline, it is a breath of fresh air, but the affair is not over: such a jump can also deflate quickly.
